label: es-e2
change: The content identity leaves NTSDCore: OriginalContentIdentity (Core) carries the reference EXE SHA, each package's manifest digest (catalog, startup, common sounds, loading interface, character menu, War menu, arenas) and the counts the manifests must declare (catalog 1198 entries, roles 521/669/8; startup 45 entries, absent files [data/ad0.txt]). OriginalContentLocation carries it; the six loaders' load(directory:identity:) and bundled(in:) check against it in the old order with the old errors; NTSD 2.4's values are NTSDContent.identity. The host requirement contentFallback (E1a) becomes contentLocation(in:), which every host answers with NTSDContent.location(in:). Structural facts of the engine's EXE model stay in Core (manifest format version, globals 0x44d000/0xc3a8, the EXE's load lists, warPaths, size bounds). Tests keep their load(directory:) calls through overloads passing NTSD's identity.
checks: debug build of every Mac target with tests and a portable headless build: no error, no new warning in the touched files

26 damaged-package loader tests (LoadingSession, StartupInputs, InterfaceInputs, MenuInputs, ConcurrentInputs, LZ4) in the debug build, including the exact-error cases: pass; after the review fix, StartupInputs and LZ4 again: pass

OriginalContentIdentity's comment states that exeSHA256 must name the EXE the engine models until a game profile (E5)
review.notes: 2.8.3.3's content origin fits as location + identity; its identity String label and partial-target shape need alignment when that branch rebases (separate branch, not touched)
